results.correct_value: Approach through Crescent Creek Basin and over the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col onto the north side; the Eye Col is where the couloir tops out, not the approach
results.evidence: The first-ascent report describes camping on the Chopping Block ridge, traversing Crescent Creek Basin and climbing through the Otto-Himmel col to reach the north side of the Twin Needles, with the couloir starting ~1000 ft below the col and ending at Eye Col. The 2011 ski-descent report likewise went from the Chopping Block camp down into Crescent Creek basin and up to the Otto-Himmel col; the 2022 AAJ note uses the same Crescent Creek Basin -> Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col -> Mustard Glacier approach to the adjacent buttress. The approach text wrongly says the route avoids Crescent Creek Basin. The bivy note's 'north side of the crest' is left to the camping clean-up.

patches.find: Approached from the north side of the Twin Needles rather than the standard Crescent Creek Basin/Eye Col south approach; specific trailhead-to-base beta beyond the first-ascent account has not been published.
patches.replace: From a camp on the Chopping Block ridge, traverse Crescent Creek Basin and climb to the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col, then descend its north side onto the Mustard Glacier; the couloir starts roughly 1,000 ft below the col and tops out at the Eye Col between the two Needles. The usual way down is by the gullies on the south side of the Eye Col back into Crescent Creek Basin.

results.correct_value: County is Whatcom; backup sheriff line not established
results.evidence: The Twin Needles are in Whatcom County (Wikipedia infobox/category, citing GNIS; the route rows themselves agree). The stored value leads with North Cascades NP dispatch and names the Skagit County Sheriff line only as an after-hours backup — the same pattern used on ~50 other Pickets rows, which a 2026-09-16 sheriff-number sweep deliberately refused to change (this exact row was named there). No agency page was found that states which sheriff line NPS uses as its after-hours backup for this part of the park, so replacing the number is not established; flagged for the owner, no patch.

results.fact: Which line this is (moderate South Route vs the II 5.10a East Arete)
results.correct_value: Probably the moderate Eye Col line (crux ~5.7), with the II 5.10a east arête a separate route; not settled by two sources
results.evidence: Two different lines are merged in this row. The 2003 AAJ account lists East Twin Needle (II 5.10a) as one of three first ascents on the east-to-west Southern Pickets traverse and describes the 'tremendously exposed east arête' — that is where the grade, rock_grade, fa, face and beta come from. Separately, the 2009 first-ascent report of Thread of Ice climbed East Twin Needle directly from the Eye Col with a crux 5.7 hand crack, and the 2022 AAJ note descended the peak's south face to the Eye Col by downclimbing and rappels — the moderate Eye Col line that overview, pro_needs, pro_tips, partner requirements and itinerary describe. Only one source grades the Eye Col line (5.7), so the row's grade/fa/face/beta cannot yet be rewritten to it with two agreeing sources; which line this row is (name 'South Route' vs the 5.10a data) is an owner decision. No patch.

results.fact: Where the east arete starts relative to the Eye Col
results.correct_value: The east arête is not gained from the Eye Col (the col is the notch on East Twin Needle's west side); the approach's last clause and climbing_route[1] belong to the other line
results.evidence: The Eye Col is the notch between East and West Twin Needle (2022 AAJ note; 2009 first-ascent report), i.e. on East Twin Needle's west side, and the 2003 party reached the east arête while traversing east to west from The Rake. So approach_variants[0].baseFinding is right and climbing_route[1]/the approach's final clause are wrong — but the correct replacement text (the Eye Col line's own description) depends on the unresolved identity question above, so no patch is written.

The 2003 party (Wallace, Haley, Bunker, July 27, 2003) is credited with East Twin Needle's II 5.10a east arête. No source names a first-ascent party for the Eye Col line; the 1932 Degenhardt party is credited with 'Twin Needles' generally (the higher West Twin). Depends on the identity decision; no patch.

results.fact: Overview says both needles were first climbed together in 1932

results.correct_value: One 60 m rope covers the Eye Col gully rappels; a second 60 m rope is needed for the double-rope rappels of the Himmelhorn-West Twin Needle notch exit
results.evidence: descent_text already distinguishes the two descents (1-3 short single-rope rappels in the Eye Col gullies; two double-60 m rappels below the Himmelhorn-West Twin notch), and gear, rack, what_to_bring, detailed_rack and rappels all carry two 60 m ropes. A 2023 West Twin Needle trip lists two 60 m ropes as essential gear and used them for the double-rope rappels past vertical slabs on that descent. Only the rope note implied a single rope was all that is needed, so it is extended rather than the rope card changed.

patches.replace: 60m rope for multi-pitch rock, plus a second 60m rope for the double-rope rappels if you descend by the Himmelhorn-West Twin Needle notch.

results.correct_value: Loose gully; small chockstones low are scrambled, larger chockstones higher are fifth class and pitched, then a short scree walk to the col
results.evidence: A 2023 party found the lower small chockstones easy, the larger ones higher 'put us in the class 5 terrain, where we needed to start pitching', and then walked up scree briefly to the Eye Col. The 2022 AAJ note descended these same south-facing gullies with repeated rappels, and the 2009 report records a chockstone rappel — not plain 4th-class ground. So the waypoint note, baseFinding and variant notes are consistent (each describes a different stretch); only the itinerary's '4th-class scrambling' understates it.

patches.find: Mix of snow and 4th-class scrambling between the two Needles.
patches.replace: Loose gully between the two Needles: small chockstones low down are scrambled, the bigger ones higher up are fifth class and usually pitched out, then a short scree walk to the col.

results.fact: Days of approach / when the climb happens
results.correct_value: One long day in to a camp on the Chopping Block ridge / Crescent Creek Basin, climb the next day, one day out
results.evidence: The 2022 AAJ party reached a col near the Chopping Block on day one (6+ miles, 6,000 ft) and climbed the next day; the 2009 first-ascent party camped on the Chopping Block ridge, climbed the next day and walked out to the car in 5 hours on day three; the 2018 Mount Terror trip was likewise 3 days. The itinerary and published times are right; partner_requirements' '~2 days each way' and the approach's mandatory 'day two' camp move are the outliers. The move to the lower 6,050 ft camp is kept as an option.

results.correct_value: Terror Creek is forded, or crossed on a big log just upstream when one is in place
results.evidence: A 2018 trip crossed at about 2,040 ft and notes a big log 500 ft upstream at 2,100 ft; a 2023 trip forded at a shallow spot; the 2011 party crossed on a long log about 15 ft above the water. The waypoint's flat 'cross on a large logjam' is too certain for a crossing that changes year to year, while the approach's 'scout for a safe crossing' is right.

results.fact: Which side of the crest Crescent Creek Basin is on
results.evidence: The approach and baseFinding are right: Crescent Creek Basin lies below the south-facing Eye Col gullies (the 2022 AAJ party descended south-facing gullies to reach it). The camp card's 'north side of the crest' is the wrong statement, but bivy[] belongs to the camping clean-up; no patch. For this route, Crescent Creek Basin camp, Stump Hollow, the Goodell roadhead and the Terror Creek roadbed spot serve the approach; Terror Basin camp is off-route (south-side base for Terror/Degenhardt); the western-crest bivouacs are marginal.
